title: Why the Police Took 78 Minutes to Stop the Uvalde Gunman

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日简讯栏目

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《DealBook》的商业与政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容为一个月的免费阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For days after the shooting in Uvalde, Texas, the explanation for how the police responded kept shifting.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州尤瓦尔迪发生枪击事件后的几天里，关于警方如何反应的解释一直在变。

sentences.en: Now, a clearer picture has emerged.
sentences.zh: 现在，一幅更清晰的画面浮出水面。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, David Goodman, on why officers waited so long before storming the classrooms where the gunman was, and the questions that raises about what happened to
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·古德曼将为我们讲述，为什么警官们在强攻枪手所在的教室之前等待了那么久，以及这引发了关于

sentences.en: the people inside.
sentences.zh: 里面的人遭遇了什么的问题。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, May 31St. David, there have been a lot of questions about the way that the police responded to the shooting in Uvalde, Texas.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月31日，星期二。大卫，关于警方对德克萨斯州尤瓦尔迪枪击事件的反应方式，有很多疑问。

sentences.en: Tell us what we know at this point.
sentences.zh: 请告诉我们目前所了解的情况。

sentences.en: Well, getting to what we know now has been really quite a journey.
sentences.zh: 好的，要弄清楚我们现在所知道的，确实经历了一波三折。

sentences.en: When the shooting happened on
sentences.zh: 当枪击事件发生在

sentences.en: Tuesday, you know, one of the first things that we wanted to try and answer after confirming that this
sentences.zh: 周二时，你知道的，在确认了这场

sentences.en: horrific event had taken place and the number of killed and wounded was, when did they finally end it?
sentences.zh: 可怕事件的发生以及死伤人数后，我们最想试图回答的问题之一是：他们究竟是什么时候结束这一切的？

sentences.en: When did they finally kill the gunman?
sentences.zh: 他们究竟是什么时候击毙枪手的？

sentences.en: And that fact was not something that they brought out immediately.
sentences.zh: 而这个事实并不是他们立刻公布的。

sentences.en: They weren't revealing that.
sentences.zh: 他们没有透露这一点。

sentences.en: And so that raised a lot of questions for me, that there was something sort of so basic that they weren't either willing or able to share.
sentences.zh: 因此这让我产生了许多疑问，竟然有如此基本的事情是他们不愿或无法分享的。

sentences.en: And so on Friday, we finally got a chance to hear directly from the state police.
sentences.zh: 所以在周五，我们终于有机会直接听到州警察的说法。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They'd been conducting the inquiry into the law enforcement response to the shooting, and they laid out their timeline in a press conference.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在对执法部门针对枪击事件的反应进行调查，并在一次新闻发布会上公布了他们的时间线。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here today.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们今天来到这里。

sentences.en: My name is Stephen McCraw, director of Texas Department of Public Safety.
sentences.zh: 我是斯蒂芬·麦克劳，德克萨斯州公共安全部主任。

sentences.en: Tell me about this press conference.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这场新闻发布会吧。

sentences.en: So Stephen McCraw, who's the head of the Texas Department of Public Safety, and this is the agency that runs the state police and also the Texas Rangers,
sentences.zh: 好的，斯蒂芬·麦克劳是德克萨斯州公共安全部的负责人，这个机构负责管理州警察和德克萨斯骑警，

sentences.en: he calls reporters to a press conference right by the elementary school.
sentences.zh: 他在小学旁边召开了一场记者会。

sentences.en: Our goal today is to provide the parents, the community of Uvalde, the public, as much information as we can, and where we are on the investigation.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的目标是向家长、尤瓦尔迪社区以及公众提供尽可能多的信息，并通报调查进展。

sentences.en: I'll begin first and foremost with the timeline, as we know it.
sentences.zh: 我首先且最重要地从我们所了解的时间线开始讲起。

sentences.en: So here's what he lays out.
sentences.zh: 以下是他列出的内容。

sentences.en: 1128, the suspect vehicle crashes into the ditch, as previously described.
sentences.zh: 11点28分，嫌疑人车辆如前所述冲进沟里。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, at about 1128 in the morning, the gunman crashes a pickup truck in a ditch that's by the school.
sentences.zh: 周二上午大约11点28分，枪手驾驶一辆皮卡车冲进学校旁边的沟里。

sentences.en: And he emerges pretty much immediately and starts shooting at the school and moving towards it.
sentences.zh: 他几乎立刻就从车里钻出来，开始向学校开枪并朝学校移动。

sentences.en: Now, at this time, a teacher calls 911 and says there's been a crash at the school and a man with a gun.
sentences.zh: 此时，一名老师拨打911报警，称学校发生了一起车祸，并且有一个带枪的男子。

sentences.en: There was a discussion early on that an ISD resource officer had confronted...
sentences.zh: 早期有一种讨论称，学区的一名资源警官曾与……

sentences.en: Now, I should say, initially, we thought or we were told that an armed school district police officer had been at the school at this time
sentences.zh: 现在我应该说明，最初我们认为或者被告知，当时学校里有一名武装的学区警察，

sentences.en: and that that armed officer had confronted the gunman.
sentences.zh: 并且这名武装警官与枪手进行了对抗。

sentences.en: That did not happen.
sentences.zh: 这并没有发生。

sentences.en: But that turned out actually not to be true.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明这其实并非事实。

sentences.en: And certainly, you know, police officers, like anyone else, under stress, sometimes witnesses get it wrong.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道的，警察和其他人一样，在压力之下，目击者有时也会弄错。

sentences.en: But the bottom line is that officer was not on scene, not on campus.
sentences.zh: 但最底线的是，那名警官不在现场，也不在校园里。

sentences.en: And instead, the gunman walks into the school through a door that's been propped open by a teacher just a short time before.
sentences.zh: 相反，枪手是通过不久前由一名老师半掩着的一扇门走进了学校。

sentences.en: And he's able to go in unchallenged and unconfronted by anyone.
sentences.zh: 他得以毫无阻碍、无人对抗地走了进去。

sentences.en: At 1133 is when the suspect entered the school at the door that I'm pointing to now.
sentences.zh: 11点33分，嫌疑人从我现在所指的这扇门进入了学校。

sentences.en: At 1133, the suspect begins shooting at the room 111 or 112.
sentences.zh: 11点33分，嫌疑人开始向111号或112号房间开枪。

sentences.en: It's not possible to determine from the...
sentences.zh: 无法从……中确定

sentences.en: He then goes into a pair of connected classrooms that are joined in the middle via a bathroom.
sentences.zh: 他随后进入了一对相连的教室，这两个教室在中间通过一间浴室连通。

sentences.en: And he starts shooting.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始开枪。

sentences.en: He shot more than 100 rounds based on the audio evidence at that time.
sentences.zh: 根据当时的声音证据，他开了一百多枪。

sentences.en: At least 100 rounds.
sentences.zh: 至少一百枪。

sentences.en: Okay, so he's shooting.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以他在开枪。

sentences.en: When did the police get inside?
sentences.zh: 警察是什么时候进去的？

sentences.en: In 1135, three police officers entered the same door as the suspect entered.
sentences.zh: 11点35分，三名警察从嫌疑人进入的同一扇门进入。

sentences.en: All three of those police officers worked for the Uvalde Police Department.
sentences.zh: 这三名警察都效力于尤瓦尔迪警察局。

sentences.en: Well, McCross says that three police officers entered the school just two minutes after the gunman had entered.
sentences.zh: 麦克劳说，三名警察在枪手进入后仅两分钟就进入了学校。

sentences.en: Those officers approached the classroom where the gunman was shooting.
sentences.zh: 这些警察走近枪手正在开枪的教室。

sentences.en: And two received grazing wounds at that time from the suspect.
sentences.zh: 当时有两名警察被嫌疑人的子弹擦伤。

sentences.en: And two of them were grazed by bullets that came through the locked classroom door.
sentences.zh: 其中两人的擦伤是由穿透上锁的教室门的子弹造成的。

sentences.en: They were later followed by another four, a team of Uvalde police officers, three, and also a county sheriff, county deputy sheriff.
sentences.zh: 随后又有另外四人跟进，这是一个由三名尤瓦尔迪警察以及一名县警长、县副警长组成的队伍。

sentences.en: Now, in the meantime, more officers were arriving on the scene.
sentences.zh: 同时，更多的警察正在赶往现场。

sentences.en: And by 1203, which is 30 minutes after the shooter had entered the classroom, there are 19 officers from different agencies gathered in the school hallway near that classroom door.
sentences.zh: 到12点03分，即枪手进入教室30分钟后，已有来自不同机构的19名警察聚集在教室门外的学校走廊里。

sentences.en: Wow, 19 officers.
sentences.zh: 哇，19名警察。

sentences.en: And what are they doing at this point?
sentences.zh: 此时他们在做什么？

sentences.en: Well, by the time those 19 officers are in the hallway, the commanding officer on the scene had made a critical decision.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当这19名警察到达走廊时，现场的指挥官做出了一个关键决定。

sentences.en: He determined that this was a situation at that point of a barricaded subject and not an active shooter.
sentences.zh: 他判定当时的情况属于有路障的嫌疑人（对峙），而非活跃枪手。

sentences.en: And so the officers were told not to try to go into that classroom.
sentences.zh: 因此警察被告知不要试图进入那个教室。

sentences.en: David, hold on.
sentences.zh: 大卫，等等。

sentences.en: What's the difference between barricaded subject and active shooter?
sentences.zh: 有路障的嫌疑人和活跃枪手有什么区别？

sentences.en: I don't understand that terminology.
sentences.zh: 我不懂这个术语。

sentences.en: I mean, how is law enforcement supposed to respond in each type of case?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在每种情况下执法部门应该如何反应？

sentences.en: So there's been a lot of law enforcement thinking around this in recent years.
sentences.zh: 近年来，执法部门围绕这一点有很多思考。

sentences.en: And in an active shooter situation, the practice is you go in immediately.
sentences.zh: 在活跃枪手的情况下，做法是立即冲进去。

sentences.en: You don't wait as soon as you have enough officers to safely do so.
sentences.zh: 只要有足够的警力安全地做到这一点，你就不能等待。

sentences.en: Or even one officer can make that determination to go in.
sentences.zh: 甚至一名警察也可以做出冲进去的决定。

sentences.en: But the important thing is that there's no hesitation.
sentences.zh: 但重要的是不能犹豫。

sentences.en: There's no waiting for special equipment or any of that.
sentences.zh: 不需要等待特殊装备或任何此类东西。

sentences.en: You go in to stop the shooting, which means to try and incapacitate or kill the shooter, and then to stop people from dying.
sentences.zh: 你冲进去是为了阻止枪击，这意味着试图使枪手丧失能力或将其击毙，然后阻止人员伤亡。

sentences.en: So you treat the wounded.
sentences.zh: 所以你要救治伤员。

sentences.en: And you do that in that order.
sentences.zh: 并且你要按这个顺序去做。

sentences.en: But the paramount important thing is to stop the shooting from happening.
sentences.zh: 但至关重要的大事是阻止枪击事件的发生。

sentences.en: So what about a barricaded subject?
sentences.zh: 那么有路障的嫌疑人呢？

sentences.en: What is that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: And how should the police respond in that kind of situation?
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下警察应该如何反应？

sentences.en: So a barricaded subject is very different.
sentences.zh: 所以有路障的嫌疑人非常不同。

sentences.en: It's someone who's armed inside a space that's hard to get into and isn't posing any kind of immediate risk to civilians at that moment.
sentences.zh: 那是指某人武装在一个难以进入的空间内，并且在那一刻对平民不构成任何直接危险。

sentences.en: But it's instead focused on keeping law enforcement away.
sentences.zh: 而是专注于将执法人员挡在外面。

sentences.en: And so the response to a barricaded subject is a lot more strategic.
sentences.zh: 因此，针对有路障的嫌疑人的反应要策略得多。

sentences.en: You know, rather than rushing in,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，与其冲进去，

sentences.en: the police are trained to go in more slowly with specialized equipment and more tactically so that they can avoid any kind of injury or any of law enforcement officers being killed.
sentences.zh: 警察受到的训练是带着专业装备和更多战术性地缓慢进入，这样他们就能避免任何伤害或任何执法人员被杀。

sentences.en: So less a focus on safety of civilians and more a focus on safety of law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 因此，关注点较少放在平民的安全上，而更多地放在执法人员的安全上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, David, this decision seems huge.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，这个决定看起来意义重大。

sentences.en: I mean, they're treating the gunman like a barricaded subject, not like an active shooter.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们把枪手当作有路障的嫌疑人对待，而不是活跃枪手。

sentences.en: And that means that they're not immediately going into the classroom.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们没有立即进入教室。

sentences.en: But do we know why they made that call?
sentences.zh: 但我们知道他们为什么做出那个决定吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's not really clear why they made that call,
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前还不清楚他们为什么做出那个决定，

sentences.en: especially because another thing that came out during the press conference was that there were kids in the classroom who were still alive, whose lives were still at risk.
sentences.zh: 特别是因为新闻发布会上透露的另一件事是，教室里还有仍然活着的孩子，他们的生命仍然处于危险之中。

sentences.en: And the way we know that is because some of them were calling 911.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这一点的途径是，其中一些孩子正在拨打911。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And now I'd like to go over the 911 timeline.
sentences.zh: 现在我想回顾一下911的时间线。

sentences.en: McCraw, during the press briefing, he starts going through a timeline of these 911 calls.
sentences.zh: 麦克劳在简报会上开始梳理这些911报警电话的时间线。

sentences.en: So I'll warn you, it's not better than I read it than you listen to it.
sentences.zh: 所以我得提醒你，我读出来并不比你听起来更好。

sentences.en: The caller identified, I'll not say her name, but she was in room 112, called 911 at 1203.
sentences.zh: 这名被识别的报警人，我不会说出她的名字，但她在112号房间，于12点03分拨打911。

sentences.en: The duration of the call was one minute and 23 seconds.
sentences.zh: 通话持续时间是一分二十三秒。

sentences.en: She identified herself and whispered, she's in room 112.
sentences.zh: 她报了名字并耳语说她在112号房间。

sentences.en: So at 1203, a student calls 911 and whispers that she's in the classroom with the gunman.
sentences.zh: 所以在12点03分，一名学生拨打911并耳语说她和枪手在同一个教室里。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And this is the exact moment that we know that 19 officers are gathered in the hallway outside the door.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所知道的19名警察聚集在门外走廊里的确切时刻。

sentences.en: Wow, crazy.
sentences.zh: 哇，太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And she calls multiple times.
sentences.zh: 而且她打了多次电话。

sentences.en: She called back in room 12, advisor, multiple dead.
sentences.zh: 她从12号房间回拨，提示有多人死亡。

sentences.en: Again, she called on the phone.
sentences.zh: 她再次通过电话呼叫。

sentences.en: Again, at 1216, she's called back and said there's eight to nine students alive.
sentences.zh: 又在12点16分，她回拨电话说有八到九名学生还活着。

sentences.en: And from these calls, it's clear from what she says that there are still some children who are alive.
sentences.zh: 从这些电话中，从她所说的话可以清楚地看出，仍有一些孩子活着。

sentences.en: And another person in room 111 calls.
sentences.zh: 111号房间的另一个人也打了电话。

sentences.en: She hung up when another student told her to hang up.
sentences.zh: 当另一个学生叫她挂断时，她挂断了电话。

sentences.en: And then at 1219, another student from one of these linked classrooms calls.
sentences.zh: 然后在12点19分，来自这些相连教室之一的另一名学生打来电话。

sentences.en: And during this time.
sentences.zh: 在此期间。

sentences.en: You can hear over the 911 call that three shots were fired.
sentences.zh: 你可以从911通话中听到传出了三声枪响。

sentences.en: McCraw says the shots are still being fired sporadically.
sentences.zh: 麦克劳说枪声仍在零星地响着。

sentences.en: And then.
sentences.zh: 然后。

sentences.en: The initial caller called back.
sentences.zh: 最初的报警人回拨了。

sentences.en: That first 911 caller, she calls back at 1243 and again at 1247 and is asking to please send in the police.
sentences.zh: 那个最初的911报警人，她在12点43分和12点47分再次回拨，请求请派警察进去。

sentences.en: Okay, so you're saying that over the course of more than 40 minutes, there are kids calling 911 from inside the classrooms, which is kind of incredible.
sentences.zh: 好的，你的意思是，在持续四十多分钟的时间里，有孩子从教室里面打911报警，这简直难以置信。

sentences.en: And it makes me think I really don't understand why at this point the officers still aren't going in.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得我真的不明白为什么到了这个时候警官们仍然不进去。

sentences.en: Well, yeah, from the press conference, it was not clear whether the officers on the scene were hearing about these 911 calls.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，从新闻发布会上来看，并不清楚现场的警察是否听到了这些911报警电话。

sentences.en: That would be a pretty serious communications breakdown in the middle of this incredibly serious event.
sentences.zh: 在如此极其严肃的事件中，这将是一次相当严重的通信中断。

sentences.en: And if the 911 operators were aware that children were alive in that classroom, why weren't officers notified of that?
sentences.zh: 如果911接线员知道教室里还有活着的儿童，为什么没有通知警察？

sentences.en: And if that's the case, why didn't they take action?
sentences.zh: 如果真是这样，他们为什么不采取行动？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: McCraw's actually asked directly about this.
sentences.zh: 实际上有人直接问了麦克劳这个问题。

sentences.en: And again, I'll go back to the answer for right now is that that it was considered.
sentences.zh: 我再次回到目前的回答，那就是这曾被考虑过。

sentences.en: Okay, the decision was made on the scene.
sentences.zh: 好吧，决定是在现场做出的。

sentences.en: I wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 我当时不在场。

sentences.en: And he didn't really answer.
sentences.zh: 而他并没有真正回答。

sentences.en: You know, a decision was made.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个决定做出了。

sentences.en: And certainly the officers who were outside the classroom, you know, they could hear the gunshots that were happening sporadically.
sentences.zh: 当然，站在教室外面的警察，你知道的，他们能听到零星发生的枪声。

sentences.en: And by this time, there are multiple law enforcement agencies there at the elementary school.
sentences.zh: 此时，小学里有多个执法机构。

sentences.en: And many of these officers were bristling, were really getting upset at the order to stand by and wait.
sentences.zh: 其中的许多警察都感到恼火，对原地待命和等待的命令感到非常不满。

sentences.en: And what's remarkable is that it's not even clear at this point to us who made the ultimate decision to go in or how that decision was reached.
sentences.zh: 而引人注目的是，目前我们甚至还不清楚究竟是谁做出了冲进去的最终决定，又是如何做出这个决定的。

sentences.en: What we do know is that 78 minutes after the shooter enters the school at about 12.50 on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，在枪手进入学校大约78分钟后，也就是周二大约12点50分。

sentences.en: They breached the door using keys that they're able to get from the janitor because both doors were locked.
sentences.zh: 他们用从工友那里拿到的钥匙破门而入，因为两扇门都锁着。

sentences.en: Officers finally go in.
sentences.zh: 警察终于冲了进去。

sentences.en: At 12.50, shots are fired.
sentences.zh: 12点50分，传出枪声。

sentences.en: They can be heard.
sentences.zh: 可以听到枪声。

sentences.en: In 9-1-1 calls, you can actually hear the shots being fired, McCroft said.
sentences.zh: 麦克克罗夫特说，在911报警电话里，你实际上能听到枪声。

sentences.en: 12.51 is very loud and sounds like the officers are moving children out of the room.
sentences.zh: 12点51分声音非常响亮，听起来像警察正在把孩子们转移出房间。

sentences.en: And we know from the police report, the shooter is killed at that moment.
sentences.zh: 我们从警方报告中得知，枪手就在那时被击毙了。

sentences.en: Questions.
sentences.zh: 问题。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载纽约时报App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订户每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订户，请立即下载《时报》App，即可免费畅读30天。

sentences.en: David, so much of the police response really hinges on that one decision, to wait to go into the classrooMs.
sentences.zh: 大卫，警方的很多应对措施实际上都取决于那一个决定，也就是等待进入教室。

sentences.en: So what do we know about the commander in charge, the guy who made the call to hold off?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们对负责的指挥官了解多少，也就是那个下令暂缓行动的人？

sentences.en: So, the guy who made the decision, his name is Pete Arradondo.
sentences.zh: 做出这个决定的人名叫皮特·阿拉东多。

sentences.en: And he's someone who has a long law enforcement career.
sentences.zh: 他有着长期的执法生涯。

sentences.en: He had been at the Uvalde Police Department.
sentences.zh: 他曾任职于尤瓦尔迪警察局。

sentences.en: He's actually from the city.
sentences.zh: 他其实就是当地人。

sentences.en: And he'd gone on to a sheriff's office in a nearby county and actually run a school police department in a different county.
sentences.zh: 后来他去了附近一个县的治安官办公室，还在另一个县担任过学校警察局局长。

sentences.en: He recently came back and started working again in Uvalde, but he wasn't the chief of the Uvalde Police Department.
sentences.zh: 他最近回来了，并在尤瓦尔迪重新开始工作，但他并不是尤瓦尔迪警察局的局长。

sentences.en: He came back as the chief of the Uvalde School District Police Department.
sentences.zh: 他回来担任的是尤瓦尔迪学区警察局局长。

sentences.en: And what's that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: That's a school police force of just six cops, including Arradondo.
sentences.zh: 那是一支只有六名警察的学校警察部队，其中包括阿拉东多。

sentences.en: And it's a structure that you actually find quite commonly in Texas and in other parts of the country, although it's not universal.
sentences.zh: 这种架构在得克萨斯州和该国其他地区其实很常见，尽管并非普遍存在。

sentences.en: But what it means is that Arradondo and his officers had jurisdiction over the campuses of the schools in Uvalde.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着阿拉东多和他的警员对尤瓦尔迪学校的校园拥有管辖权。

sentences.en: And there were eight different schools.
sentences.zh: 那里有八所不同的学校。

sentences.en: And so these six officers would either stay at the schools or go between them and provide security for those schools.
sentences.zh: 因此，这六名警察要么驻守在学校里，要么在学校之间奔波，为这些学校提供安保。

sentences.en: So it's like a tiny police force literally for the school system.
sentences.zh: 所以它就像是专门为学校系统设立的一支微型警察部队。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But why did this chief have the ultimate say?
sentences.zh: 但为什么这位局长拥有最终决定权呢？

sentences.en: I mean, why not, for example, the police chief of the city of Uvalde, who I assume has a bigger police force?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么不是例如尤瓦尔迪市的警察局长呢？我猜他的警力规模更大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a good question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: And it would seem from the outside that you would want, of course, the police department of the city to run a scene like this.
sentences.zh: 从外表来看，你当然会希望由城市警察局来指挥这样的现场。

sentences.en: But in fact, really, the reason is that the shooting is happening on the campus of the schools.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，原因在于枪击事件发生在学校校园里。

sentences.en: And that's the jurisdiction of this police chief.
sentences.zh: 那是这位警察局长的管辖范围。

sentences.en: And, you know, other departments in these kinds of situations will come into the incident.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，在这种情况下，其他部门也会介入这起事件。

sentences.en: There are officers arriving from all different kinds of agencies.
sentences.zh: 来自各种不同机构的警察都在赶到现场。

sentences.en: And you need to have some kind of hierarchy and organization.
sentences.zh: 你需要某种层级和组织结构。

sentences.en: And it generally falls to the person who has a jurisdiction to maintain that control over the scene until they hand it off.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，由拥有管辖权的人来维持对现场的控制，直到他们移交权力为止。

sentences.en: Now, they don't have to hand it off.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也可以不移交。

sentences.en: And in this case, the chief of the school district police didn't hand it off.
sentences.zh: 在本案中，学区警察局局长并没有移交指挥权。

sentences.en: And it's not clear whether anyone tried to take it away from him or at least assert any kind of control when there were clearly disagreements among the officers about the tactics that were being used.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚是否有人试图剥夺他的指挥权，或者至少在警察们对所使用的战术显然存在分歧时主张某种控制权。

sentences.en: And what are the consequences of that decision he made, David?
sentences.zh: 大卫，他做出的那个决定会带来什么后果？

sentences.en: I mean, do we know if anyone died who might not have had the police come in earlier?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们知道是否有人如果警察早点进去就不会死吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's really difficult for us to say.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实很难说。

sentences.en: But what we do know is that the vast majority of the gunshots inside those two connected classrooms came in the very start of the attack.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实知道，那两间相连的教室里绝大多数的枪声都发生在袭击刚开始的时候。

sentences.en: And we know that the two girls who called 911, those two girls survived.
sentences.zh: 我们知道拨打911的那两个女孩，她们两个活了下来。

sentences.en: But what we don't know is whether any of those gunshots that were heard after the initial burst, if any of those hit any people inside the room.
sentences.zh: 但我们不知道的是，在最初的枪击爆发后听到的那些枪声中，是否有任何枪声击中了房间里的任何人。

sentences.en: And we also don't know whether any of the children or the two teachers who were inside of these two classrooms,
sentences.zh: 我们也不知道这两间教室里的任何孩子或两名老师，

sentences.en: whether they would have survived if police had gotten in there and killed this gunman sooner and allowed them to get medical attention much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 如果警察早点冲进去击毙枪手，并让他们更快地得到医疗救助，他们是否能幸存下来。

sentences.en: And during this press conference, you know, McCraw has pressed multiple times about the order,
sentences.zh: 在这次新闻发布会上，你知道，麦克克罗多次被问及关于这项命令的问题，

sentences.en: about the decision to treat this scene in a way that even those officers thought was not correct.
sentences.zh: 关于那种处理现场的方式的决定，连那些警察自己都认为是不正确的。

sentences.en: Hey, for the benefit of hindsight, where I'm sitting now, of course it was not the right decision.
sentences.zh: 嘿，事后诸葛亮来看，以我现在的立场，这当然不是正确的决定。

sentences.en: It was the wrong decision, period.
sentences.zh: 这是错误的决定，毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: And McCraw acknowledged, he says, this had been the wrong decision.
sentences.zh: 麦克克罗也承认了，他说，这是一个错误的决定。

sentences.en: There's no excuse for that.
sentences.zh: 这没有任何借口。

sentences.en: But again, I wasn't there, but I'm just telling you, from what we know, we believe there should have been an entry of that as soon as you can.
sentences.zh: 但话又说回来，我当时不在现场，不过我只是告诉你们，从我们所了解的情况来看，我们认为只要可能就应该尽快突入。

sentences.en: Hey, when there's an active shooter, the rules change.
sentences.zh: 嘿，当有现行枪手时，规则就变了。

sentences.en: You don't have to have a leader on the scene.
sentences.zh: 你不需要在现场有一个领导。

sentences.en: Every officer lines up, stacks up, goes and finds where those rounds are being fired at and keeps shooting until the subject is dead, period.
sentences.zh: 每个警察都要排好队，集结起来，去找出那些子弹是从哪里射出来的，然后不断开枪，直到嫌疑人死亡，毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: It seems like a pretty big deal for law enforcement to admit that they were wrong.
sentences.zh: 对于执法部门来说，承认自己错了似乎是一件大事。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No, it's not about trying to defend or it's not about trying to assess or even be hypercritical.
sentences.zh: 不，这不是为了辩护，也不是为了评估甚至进行过度批判。

sentences.en: It's about the facts and sharing whatever we learn on the facts as quick as we can.
sentences.zh: 这是关于事实，并尽我们所能以最快的速度分享我们在事实上了解到的任何情况。

sentences.en: You know, McCraw says several times that he's not there to place blame.
sentences.zh: 你知道，麦克克罗多次表示他不是来推卸责任的。

sentences.en: But in the end, he does end up rendering a judgment on the police response.
sentences.zh: 但最终，他还是对警方的应对做出了评判。

sentences.en: David, on the one hand, focusing on the police response makes sense, right?
sentences.zh: 大卫，一方面，关注警方的应对是有道理的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because if something faster would have prevented even one of those deaths, we'd want to know that.
sentences.zh: 因为如果行动更快一点能挽救哪怕其中一条生命，我们也会希望知道这一点。

sentences.en: But I guess I'm wondering, is that the right focus?
sentences.zh: 但我想我在想的是，这真的是正确的焦点吗？

sentences.en: Because it sounds like even if the police had gone in earlier, it might not have made that much difference.
sentences.zh: 因为听起来，即使警察早点进去，可能也不会有多大区别。

sentences.en: I mean, as you said, most of the rounds were fired in the first few minutes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如你所说，大部分子弹都是在前几分钟发射的。

sentences.en: So I guess what I'm wondering is, are we missing the bigger picture?
sentences.zh: 所以我想我在想的是，我们是不是忽略了更大的全貌？

sentences.en: You know, that an 18-year-old who is determined to shoot up a school can legally buy two very powerful guns and do it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个决心血洗学校的18岁年轻人可以合法购买两把威力巨大的枪并付诸行动。

sentences.en: Well, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a lot easier, especially in Texas, to focus on something like the police response than it is to focus on the guns that were used.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特别是在得克萨斯州，把焦点放在警方的应对上，要比把焦点放在所使用的枪支上容易得多。

sentences.en: And you've seen this after several major shootings in the last few years here in Texas.
sentences.zh: 你在过去几年这里得克萨斯州发生的几起重大枪击事件后都看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You've had Sutherland Springs in 2017.
sentences.zh: 2017年发生过萨瑟兰斯普林斯枪击案。

sentences.en: That was at a church.
sentences.zh: 那是在一座教堂里。

sentences.en: You had a school shooting in 2018 in the town of Santa Fe where 10 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 2018年在圣达菲镇发生了一起学校枪击案，造成10人死亡。

sentences.en: And you had a gunman shoot multiple people inside a Walmart in El Paso in 2019.
sentences.zh: 2019年，一名枪手在埃尔帕索的一家沃尔玛超市内枪杀多人。

sentences.en: And throughout that time and afterwards, the state has actually moved in the direction of making it easier to own and carry weapons in the state,
sentences.zh: 在那期间以及之后，该州实际上一直在朝着让在州内拥有和携带武器变得更容易的方向发展，

sentences.en: including last year when they passed a law to allow any Texan or pretty much any Texan over 21 to carry a handgun without a permit.
sentences.zh: 包括去年他们通过了一项法律，允许任何得克萨斯州人或几乎任何21岁以上的得克萨斯州人在无需许可证的情况下携带手枪。

sentences.en: And so the move here is really to look for other solutions.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的举措实际上是寻找其他解决办法。

sentences.en: It's really anything other than preventing an 18-year-old from buying a weapon.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是除了阻止18岁年轻人买枪之外的任何办法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like we talk about police response and these other things because that's one of the few things on the table we actually can talk about.
sentences.zh: 就像我们讨论警方的应对和其他事情一样，因为这是我们实际上可以讨论的少数几件事情之一。

sentences.en: Because in Texas, we're not going to talk about gun control.
sentences.zh: 因为在得克萨斯州，我们是不会讨论枪支管制的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: what you see right now is that there's agreement among Democrats and some Republicans that these officers should have done more during that hour to try and stop the shooter.
sentences.zh: 你现在看到的是，民主党人和一些共和党人达成了一致，认为这些警察在那一个小时里本应该采取更多行动来试图阻止枪手。

sentences.en: That's something that pretty much everybody can agree on.
sentences.zh: 这是几乎所有人都能达成一致的看法。

sentences.en: Something went wrong here in that response.
sentences.zh: 那天的应对中确实出了问题。

sentences.en: And that's a conversation that people are willing to have.
sentences.zh: 这是人们愿意进行的对话。

sentences.en: And I think the conversation that people in Texas and elsewhere find it much more difficult to have is the question of why that 18-year-old was able to buy that gun and walk into the school to begin with.
sentences.zh: 我认为得克萨斯州及其他地方的人们发现更难进行的对话是：为什么那个18岁年轻人能够买到那把枪并一开始就走进学校的问题。

sentences.en: David, thank you.
sentences.zh: 大卫，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周末，美国

sentences.en: Department of Justice said it would review the police response to the mass shooting in Uvalde.
sentences.zh: 司法部表示将审查警方对尤瓦尔迪大规模枪击案的应对措施。

sentences.en: The DOJ said it was conducting the review at the request of Uvalde's mayor and that the goal was to provide an independent account of the response that day and to identify lessons learned and best practices.
sentences.zh: 司法部表示，该审查是应尤瓦尔迪市长的要求进行的，其目的是对那天的应对提供独立的说明，并找出经验教训和最佳做法。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Monday, European Union leaders reached a compromise to impose a partial ban on Russian oil.
sentences.zh: 周一，欧盟领导人达成妥协，对俄罗斯石油实施部分禁令。

sentences.en: The embargo had been blocked by Hungary, an EU member, so leaders limited it, exempting pipeline imports, in order to get Hungary to go along with it.
sentences.zh: 该禁令此前一直遭到欧盟成员国匈牙利的阻挠，因此领导人缩小了禁令范围，免除了管道进口，以让匈牙利予以配合。

sentences.en: The embargo is likely to hurt European economies and is the latest sign that Europe is willing to take far-reaching steps to punish Russia.
sentences.zh: 该禁令可能会损害欧洲经济，这也是欧洲愿意采取影响深远的措施来惩罚俄罗斯的最新迹象。

sentences.en: And As a government, as a society, we have a responsibility to act to prevent more tragedies.
sentences.zh: 作为一个政府，作为一个社会，我们有责任采取行动防止更多的悲剧发生。

sentences.en: Legislation introduced in Canada would require most owners of military-style assault weapons to turn over their guns to a government buyback program.
sentences.zh: 加拿大提出的立法将要求大多数军用突击武器的所有者将枪支交还给政府回购计划。

sentences.en: The Canadian government also imposed new regulations banning the sale, purchase, transfer, and importation of handguns.
sentences.zh: 加拿大政府还实施了新的法规，禁止销售、购买、转让和进口手枪。

sentences.en: This is about freedom.
sentences.zh: 这关乎自由。

sentences.en: People should be free to go to the supermarket, their school, or their place of worship without fear.
sentences.zh: 人们应该有自由去超市、学校或礼拜场所，而不用担惊受怕。

sentences.en: These people should be free to go to the park or to a birthday party without worrying about what might happen from a stray bullet.
sentences.zh: 这些人应该有自由去公园或参加生日派对，而不必担心流弹可能会带来的后果。

sentences.en: The legislation is expected to pass, and the changes will apply to tens of thousands of firearMs.
sentences.zh: 该立法预计将获得通过，这些变化将适用于数万支枪械。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科和斯特拉·陈制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by M.J.
sentences.zh: 由M.J.

sentences.en: Davis-Lynn and Lisa Chow with help from Paige Cowett.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯-林恩和莉萨·乔编辑，佩奇·考维特提供了帮助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marianne Lozano and was engineered by Corey Shruppel.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽安·洛扎诺的原创音乐，由科里·施鲁佩尔工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Bumberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·邦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日纪事》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《导购秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人在家一样舒适的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是深度睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会晕厥过去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在纽约时报App或你喜欢收听的任何地方找到《导购秀》。
